note: Author's recommended discovery questionnaire. The areas follow the requirement groups in Engineering AI Systems ch. 12 (data, infrastructure, operations, quality) plus the user's list of workload, scale, skills, compliance, budget and timeline. Weights and thresholds are heuristics, not published rules.

questions.text: Is there one named person who can approve the budget and the go decision?
questions.why: A workshop without a decision maker produces a document nobody can act on.

questions.text: Can real end users join the workshop and review PoC output?
questions.why: Engineering AI Systems ch. 12 names end-user involvement a key success factor.

questions.text: Has the customer tried this before, and how did it end?
questions.why: In the Fraunhofer case the client had a failed earlier PoC and wanted to see what differed.

questions.text: State the use case in one sentence and name the person whose work changes.
questions.why: Everything else is sized from this sentence.

questions.text: Do people wait for the answer, or does it run in the background?
questions.why: Interactive work needs latency targets and headroom. Batch work needs throughput and a deadline.

questions.text: How many requests or jobs run at the same time at the busiest moment?
questions.why: Sizing follows the peak, not the average.

questions.text: What response time do users call acceptable, in seconds at the 95th percentile?
questions.why: This becomes a PoC success criterion.

questions.text: Will the model run on the customer's own hardware, or through a hosted API?
questions.why: In the Fraunhofer case the client had ruled out cloud-hosted models, which shaped every later choice.

questions.text: Where does the data live today?
questions.why: Data gravity decides where compute can sit.

questions.text: How much data does the use case read, in GB?
questions.why: Sizes storage and the ingest path.

questions.text: Has anyone measured the quality of this data, or is it a belief?
questions.why: In the Fraunhofer PoC the bulk of the work went into parsing and preprocessing the input.

questions.text: Do correct answers exist that we can score the system against?
questions.why: Without ground truth a PoC cannot show success.

questions.text: Does the data contain personal or regulated information?
questions.why: Drives isolation, logging and where the model may run.

questions.text: How many GPUs does the customer operate today?
questions.why: Zero means the team has no GPU operations history.

questions.text: How many times higher is the peak than the average load?
questions.why: A high ratio makes average-based sizing fail.

questions.text: What availability target does the business expect, in percent?
questions.why: Sets redundancy and on-call needs.

questions.text: How many people will operate the platform after handover?
questions.why: The design must fit the team that will own it.

questions.text: How much Kubernetes experience does the team have?
questions.why: Decides managed service versus self-built.

questions.text: Has the team run GPU workloads in production?
questions.why: GPU failure modes are different from CPU ones.

questions.text: Does an on-call rotation exist today?
questions.why: Handover is empty without someone who answers the page.

questions.text: Must the data stay in a named country or on the customer's premises?
questions.why: Can rule out hosted APIs and some regions.

questions.text: Is an audit trail of who asked what required?
questions.why: Affects logging design and retention.

questions.text: How many weeks does the security and legal approval take?
questions.why: Approval time often exceeds build time.

questions.text: Is there a fixed budget, a range, or no number yet?
questions.why: An unknown budget means the options cannot be ranked.

questions.text: Does finance prefer buying hardware or paying monthly?
questions.why: Machine Learning Platform Engineering ch. 1 frames build versus buy as a real choice.

questions.text: Which vendor contracts or commitments already exist?
questions.why: Existing commitments constrain the options.

questions.text: How many weeks until the customer wants real users on a pilot?
questions.why: The deadline decides how much can be built versus bought.

questions.text: How many weeks can the PoC run before a go or no-go decision?
questions.why: The PoC window must be long enough to collect repeated measurements.

questions.text: What causes the deadline: a contract, an event, or a wish?
questions.why: Separates a hard date from a soft one.

risk_rules.message: No decision maker named. Get one before the PoC starts.
End users cannot join. Reviews of PoC output will be second hand.
A previous attempt failed. Ask what was different about the goals and the data.
Residency is required but the plan uses a hosted API. The two conflict.
No ground truth. The PoC cannot prove success. Create a scored sample first.
Data quality is unknown. Budget PoC time for data inspection.
No GPU operations experience and no GPUs today. Plan training or a managed service.
Availability target is 99.9 or higher but no on-call exists.
Peak is more than 5 times the average. Size for the peak and ask what can be queued.
Approval takes longer than the time to pilot. The date is not reachable as stated.
PoC window under 4 weeks. Repeated measurements may not fit.
Budget unknown. Options cannot be ranked by cost.
Team of fewer than 3 operators will own the platform. Favour managed components.
Personal data present and audit logging not required. Confirm that with the compliance owner.
